about.title: Weed Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Weed is a small Siskiyou County community, and many residents rely on a limited number of local clinics and the nearest regional hospitals for care, which can mean fewer specialists reviewing a difficult case before something goes wrong. When a delayed diagnosis, medication mix-up, or surgical error causes real harm, the aftermath often involves confusing medical records, insurance pushback, and questions about whether the outcome was truly preventable. California treats medical malpractice claims differently than a typical injury case — MICRA sets specific notice periods, statute-of-limitations rules, and caps on certain damages, and a qualified medical expert almost always has to weigh in before a claim can move forward. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply help Weed residents get in touch, free of charge, with an independent attorney who can review the medical records, explain whether MICRA's rules apply to your situation, and help you understand what steps might come next.

whyChoose.title: Why Weed Patients Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand the MICRA Clock
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the harm and no more than three years from the injury itself to act, and a 90-day pre-suit notice is often required first. An attorney can help you figure out where you stand before those deadlines pass.

items.title: A Medical Expert Usually Has to Weigh In
items.desc: Because a qualified expert almost always has to confirm that care fell below the accepted standard, having a knowledgeable attorney early can make that process smoother. We connect you with someone who works with these requirements regularly.

items.title: No Upfront Cost, No Risk
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. That structure lets you get informed answers about a possible claim without adding financial pressure while you're already dealing with a medical setback.

items.question: Does a bad medical outcome automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. California law is clear that a poor result alone isn't proof of negligence — the care has to have fallen below what a reasonably careful provider would have done. That's part of why a medical expert review is typically required before a claim can proceed.

items.question: Weed is a small town with limited medical facilities — does that affect my claim?
items.answer: It can factor into the conversation, since care sometimes involves referrals to providers or hospitals outside Siskiyou County, which may add parties or records to review. An attorney can help sort out which facilities and providers were involved and how that affects your claim.

items.question: How long do I actually have to bring a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discover (or reasonably should have discovered) the harm, but never more than three years from the date of the injury itself. There's also typically a 90-day notice requirement before filing suit, so it helps to get guidance sooner rather than later.
